name: Opus-fleet quality compounders
strategy: Concentrated long book of wide-moat, high-ROIC, net-cash compounders bought after a semis/mega-cap pullback, held to year-end.

positions.thesis: Wide-moat enterprise software + Azure/AI; fortress balance sheet, mid-40s ROIC, durable double-digit FCF growth.
Search/YouTube ad monopoly economics, net cash, cheapest of the megacaps on FCF; Gemini/Cloud optionality underpriced.
Payments network duopoly with ~90% gross margins, toll-road ROIC, secular cash-to-card tailwind, minimal capital intensity.
Membership-flywheel retail moat, pricing power, recession-resilient traffic; consistent comps and renewal rates near 93%.
Second leg of the payments duopoly; high-teens revenue growth, exceptional ROIC and buyback cadence, fortress margins.
Custom-silicon and networking moat levered to AI datacenter buildout plus sticky VMware software; strong FCF conversion after -9% 1m semis reset.
CUDA-ecosystem moat and AI-compute standard; net cash, extreme ROIC. Buying the -9% monthly SMH pullback in the category leader.
GLP-1 duopoly with multi-year capacity-constrained demand; pricing power, high ROIC, best-in-class pharma pipeline moat.
Installed-base + services moat, brand pricing power, prodigious buybacks and cash generation; ballast quality compounder.
MSCI USA quality-factor ETF as a diversified high-ROIC/low-leverage anchor to smooth single-name risk.

outlook: Broad market is extended (SPY +22.7% 12m) but leadership has narrowed and semis/megacap tech just took a 1m breather (XLK -5.2, SMH -8.7), offering better entry into the highest-quality franchises. I favor businesses that compound through any macro path via pricing power, network effects, and net-cash balance sheets, so a soft second half still leaves the book resilient. Kept the book fully long and hedge-free because the style mandate rewards owning wide-moat compounders, not timing; the 7% cash cushion (4% APY) funds weekly rebalancing and dampens drawdowns. Main risks: further AI-capex derating hitting NVDA/AVGO and rate/regulatory shocks to payments; all remain best-in-class holds into year-end.
